items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to requiring victims of
firearm violence be offered and/or provided psychiatric care
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5894

SPONSOR: BAILEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to requiring victims
of firearm violence be offered and/or provided psychiatric care

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA:

The purpose of this bill is to afford victims of gun violence an oppor-
tunity to receive psychiatric care in connection with their trauma.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill sets forth the mechanism through which a victim
of firearm violence may elect to receive psychiatric care in connection
with the traumatic event they've just experienced. In addition to defin-
ing the term "firearm violence," the bill would require that hospitals,
among other things, develop a comprehensive plan for handling such cases
(including training all relevant staff).  The bill would also require
the promulgation of such rules and regulations as may be necessary to
carry out the purpose of this new law.

Section two of the bill sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

It is estimated that tens of thousands of people survive gun violence
every year, only to endure lasting physical, emotional, and behavioral
trauma. Survivors often develop a host of psychiatric disorders, includ-
ing acute stress and post-traumatic stress disorder.  The purpose of
this bill is to give survivors an opportunity to consult with a mental
health professional immediately after such a traumatic event so they may
begin the long, arduous road to recovery.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATION FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or
repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation of
this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and completed
on or before such effective date.
